subject.title: feat: enable the new exec approvals pipeline behind an opt-in setting

question: Should the release expose the new exec-approvals execution path through a manually edited, default-off setting before interactive prompt and Settings UI support are available?
rationale: Tests and real gateway/MXC proof establish the implementation behavior, but they cannot decide whether the temporary deny/fallback-only operator experience and alternate command-authorization boundary match the intended rollout policy.

options.title: Approve opt-in rollout
options.body: Accept the hidden default-off setting as an advanced preview while retaining fail-closed behavior and tracking the prompt and Settings UI as follow-up work.

options.title: Wait for complete approval UX
options.body: Hold this PR until interactive prompting, discoverable configuration, diagnostics, and in-product recovery are available together.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in rollout
recommendation.body: Accept the hidden default-off setting as an advanced preview while retaining fail-closed behavior and tracking the prompt and Settings UI as follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: Their prior involvement with `system.run` security policy and the V2 approval direction makes them the strongest available owner for this boundary decision.
